SAASMIG_SUBTITLE: Find, suggest and apply what a TM1 v11 model needs before IBM's migration utility moves it to TM1 v12 — on PA as a Service or a local install — and check the TM1 12 database afterwards.
SAASMIG_OVERVIEWEMPTY: Pick the v11 database to migrate in Database, then Scan model. The scan shows what will not compile on TM1 12 after the migration, what will break at run time, and what can be fixed here.
SAASMIG_V12SOURCE: This is a TM1 v12 database. The scan shows what still breaks after migration (MDX, file paths, removed control objects, removed functions in processes created since); CloudID preparation is a v11 step.
SAASMIG_V12CHECKHELP: Dry-runs every process of this model against the TM1 v12 compiler of another connected database. Nothing is saved there. A process the v12 compiler rejects migrates, but does not compile or run on TM1 12. About 4 seconds per process on PA as a Service.
SAASMIG_DEPRECATEDONLY: will not compile on TM1 12, and callers
SAASMIG_NOTADMIN: Apply, CloudID changes and restore need an admin session.
SAASMIG_BULKTITLE: Apply the fixes to the selected objects?
SAASMIG_LIVEWARNING: This changes the live v11 model, which behaves differently from now until cutover — each finding says how.
SAASMIG_BULKBLOCKED: cannot be fixed automatically and are skipped
SAASMIG_BACKUPNOTE: The original of everything changed is saved first as a backup file in your Downloads folder; the Backups tab restores it. Each process is dry-run compiled before it is written, compiled after, and put back if anything fails. The run stops at the first failure.
SAASMIG_BULKV12: Each fix is also dry-run compiled on
SAASMIG_TRUNCATED: Showing the first 1,500 findings; filter to see the rest.
SAASMIG_APPSNOTE: Tick "Show TM1 Applications" to list these findings one by one.
SAASMIG_REFUSED: Apply leaves this process alone: taking the statement out would break the lines below, which still use what it sets. Change those lines (or this one) by hand, then scan again.
SAASMIG_NOTFIXABLE: Not fixable automatically: a statement that must go is part of an IF or WHILE condition.
SAASMIG_NOTHINGTOAPPLY: Nothing to change automatically; see the suggestion.
SAASMIG_APPLIEDMANUAL: fixed, re-read and compiled — needs manual work after cutover
SAASMIG_REREADMISMATCH: Read back differs from what was written:

SAASMIG_CLOUDHELP: IBM's migration utility reads a CloudID element in the }ClientProperties dimension of the v11 model. Once the element exists, only clients with a CloudID value are migrated — under that name, with their private views and subsets. Without the element everyone migrates under their current name. IBM does not specify the value format; it has to match the user's identity in the new environment (typically the IBMid e-mail). Clients whose names are CAM IDs can instead take their e-mail address with the utility's --extract-cam-emails option.
SAASMIG_CLOUDV12: CloudID works on the v11 model only: it is prepared there, before the migration reads it. TM1 v12 has no }ClientProperties, so this tab reads and writes nothing here. Open it on the v11 database.
SAASMIG_CLOUDMISSING: This model has no CloudID element.
SAASMIG_CLOUDMISSINGHELP: Create it, then fill in a value for every client that should be migrated.
SAASMIG_CLOUDCREATECONFIRM: From the moment this element exists, the migration utility migrates only clients with a CloudID value. Every client left blank — and all of their private views and subsets — will be dropped. Create it now?
SAASMIG_CLOUDDUPS: Duplicate CloudID — two clients would become one:
SAASMIG_CLOUDBLANKS: clients have no CloudID and will not be migrated.
SAASMIG_CLOUDADMIN: Admin has no CloudID: its private views and subsets will not move.
SAASMIG_CLOUDNOTEMAIL: values do not look like an e-mail address (a warning only — IBM does not specify the format).
SAASMIG_BACKUPSHELP: Every Apply and every CloudID write saves the original first, as a JSON file in your Downloads folder. Restore puts those originals back on the database they came from.

SAASMIG_COMPARETITLE: Compare with the TM1 v12 database
SAASMIG_COMPAREHELP: After the restore, lists what exists in this v11 model and not in the v12 database: those objects were not migrated (a name the utility rejects, a rejected dimension, a failed step). SAASMIG_TARGETNOTV12: That database is not TM1 v12, so it cannot be the target.

SAASMIG_V12SUMNOTRUNV11: Not run; needs a TM1 12 database connected in Arc
SAASMIG_V12CHECKSELF: Compile every process on this database
SAASMIG_COMPAREV11TITLE: Compare with the original v11 database
SAASMIG_COMPAREV11HELP: Lists what the v11 database had before the migration and this TM1 v12 database does not: those objects were not migrated. Missing processes are scanned in v11, so each one shows what it calls that TM1 12 does not have. A process that was migrated but does not compile is found by the compile check above, not here.
SAASMIG_SOURCENOTV11: That database is already TM1 v12; pick the v11 database this one was migrated from.
SAASMIG_MISSINGFROMV11: in v11 but missing here, from
SAASMIG_BEDROCKNOTE: Tick "Show Bedrock processes" to list these findings one by one.
SAASMIG_SCANFIRST: Scan the model first: this tab works from the scan.
SAASMIG_APPSHELP: TM1 Applications (Contributor) does not exist in TM1 v12. Retiring it means deleting every }tp_* object — chores, processes, views, subsets, cubes and dimensions — and the control objects TM1 keeps for them. Nothing is deleted before a backup of every selected object has been saved: definitions, cube cells and attribute values.
SAASMIG_APPSNONE: No TM1 Applications objects (}tp_*) in this model.
SAASMIG_APPSNONELEFT: No TM1 Applications objects (}tp_*) are left in this model, but {n} objects below still name one. They fail when they run: change or retire them.
SAASMIG_APPSNONELEFT1: No TM1 Applications objects (}tp_*) are left in this model, but the object below still names one. It fails when it runs: change or retire it.
SAASMIG_APPSBACKUPNOTE: A backup of every selected object is read and saved to the Downloads folder first; if it cannot be read in full, nothing is deleted, except cells TM1 refuses to let this session read (they are listed, and need a tick). The Backups tab restores it. Control objects (}ElementAttributes_, }CellSecurity_, }Subsets_ …) are in the backup for reference but are not restored: TM1 recreates them with their parent.
SAASMIG_APPSUSESWARN: objects outside TM1 Applications still point into it (listed on the right). They break once it is gone.
SAASMIG_APPSUSESHELP: These objects are not TM1 Applications but name one of its objects. Change or retire them too, or they fail after the clean-up.
SAASMIG_BEDROCKHELP: Bedrock 5 is the Bedrock release for TM1 v12. This compares every Bedrock process (}bedrock.*, and Bedrock 3's bedrock.*) with the Bedrock 5 code, upgrades the ones in use, installs the Bedrock 5 processes callers need and the database lacks, and deletes the ones nothing uses. A process is in use when a business process or a chore runs it, directly or through other Bedrock processes in use.
SAASMIG_BEDROCKV11: This is TM1 v11. Bedrock 5 runs only on TM1 v12, so the upgrade, the installs and the caller updates run on the v12 database after the migration: open this tab there. Delete the unused Bedrock processes now, though: they would migrate only to fail to compile on TM1 12 (Bedrock 4 calls removed functions), and every one deleted here is one less broken process to upgrade or explain there.
SAASMIG_BEDROCKBUNDLED: The copy bundled with this plugin
SAASMIG_BEDROCKBUNDLEDNOTE: The bundled copy is bedrock-5 at commit
SAASMIG_BEDROCKTRYBUNDLED: If GitHub cannot be reached from here, choose the bundled copy.
SAASMIG_BEDROCKNOREF: Load Bedrock 5 to see which processes are already Bedrock 5. Until then only the version the code states is shown, and that text is not reliable.
SAASMIG_BEDROCKNONE: No Bedrock processes in this model, and none called.
SAASMIG_BEDROCKDYNAMIC: business processes run a process whose name is worked out while they run (a variable or parameter the code cannot resolve), so they might run a Bedrock process without naming it. This does not mean they do: check the calls below before deleting.
SAASMIG_BRCONFIRM: Every process this touches is backed up to the Downloads folder first; the Backups tab restores it. An upgrade overwrites any local change made to that Bedrock process. Each write is dry-run compiled first, re-read and compiled after, and undone if either fails. Callers of a process whose upgrade failed are left alone.
SAASMIG_BRCALLERSHELP: Bedrock 5 dropped two parameters of }bedrock.cube.data.copy and changed the defaults of several others. A caller that relied on an old default gets it passed explicitly, so it keeps the behaviour it had; a removed parameter is dropped from the call. Each changed statement gets a # SAASMIG line saying what changed.
SAASMIG_BRCALLERSV11: These are applied on the TM1 v12 database, together with the upgrade.
SAASMIG_BACKUPREADFAILED: The backup of {name} could not be read, so nothing was changed.
SAASMIG_CALLEEFAILED: Not updated: the change to {name} failed.
SAASMIG_RESTORECONTROL: control object: TM1 recreates it with its parent
SAASMIG_RESTORENOCELLS: restored without its cells: this session could not read them when the backup was taken
SAASMIG_RESTORENOATTRS: restored without its {n} attributes: the dimension has no elements, and TM1 allows no attribute on an empty dimension (it could hold no value)
SAASMIG_APPSUNREADABLE: of the selected objects could not be checked for data: TM1 refuses this session a read of their cells, even as an admin. That does not mean they hold any, only that the plugin cannot tell. The backup keeps their definitions, and a restore brings them back without cells:
SAASMIG_APPSUNREADABLEACK: Delete them anyway; any cells they hold are not in the backup
SAASMIG_RESTORENATIVEVIEW: native view: recreate it by hand from the backup file
SAASMIG_RESTOREEXISTS: exists already: left as it is
SAASMIG_BRSETDEFAULTHELP: Set every row back to what this tab suggests: upgrade the Bedrock processes in use that are not Bedrock 5 yet, delete the ones nothing uses, leave the rest.
SAASMIG_BRL_CURRENT: Same code as Bedrock 5. Nothing to do.
SAASMIG_BRL_OUTDATED: Older or locally changed code. Upgrade replaces it with Bedrock 5, after a backup.
SAASMIG_BRL_V3: An old bedrock.* name from Bedrock 3. Its Bedrock 5 successor is shown under the name; install that and change the callers by hand.
SAASMIG_BRL_UNKNOWN: A }bedrock.* name that Bedrock 5 does not have: a custom process with the Bedrock prefix, or a retired one. Only Leave or Delete.
SAASMIG_BRL_NOTLOADED: Bedrock 5 is not loaded, so nothing is compared. If GitHub cannot be reached, choose the bundled copy.
SAASMIG_BRL_MISSING: A process in use calls it, and this database does not have it. Install adds the Bedrock 5 version (TM1 12 only).
SAASMIG_BRL_FAILSV12: Calls a function TM1 12 does not have, so it does not compile here. Upgrade to Bedrock 5 fixes it.
SAASMIG_BRL_FAILSV11: Calls a function TM1 12 does not have: it migrates, but does not compile there. Upgrade it to Bedrock 5 on TM1 12 after the migration — or delete it now if nothing uses it.
SAASMIG_BRLEGENDMORE: Every status, explained in the guide
SAASMIG_BRTIP_FAILSV12: Calls {fns}, which TM1 12 does not have, so it does not compile here.
SAASMIG_BRTIP_FAILSV11: Calls {fns}, which TM1 12 does not have: it migrates, but does not compile there.
SAASMIG_BRTIP_FIXEDBY5: The Bedrock 5 version does not call them: Upgrade fixes it.
SAASMIG_CHIPCLICK: Click to show only these; click again to show all.
SAASMIG_SEVTIP_BLOCKER: BLOCKER: does not work on TM1 12. A process that calls a function TM1 12 does not have migrates, but does not compile or run there. A name the utility rejects, or a dimension with an element-type conflict, is not migrated at all.
SAASMIG_SEVTIP_BLOCKERV12: BLOCKER: this process calls a function TM1 12 does not have, so it does not compile or run here.
SAASMIG_SEVTIP_BREAKS: BREAKS: migrates, but fails or silently returns something different on TM1 12 — MDX, file paths, removed control objects.
SAASMIG_SEVTIP_BREAKSV12: BREAKS: compiles, but fails or silently returns something different when it runs — MDX, file paths, removed control objects.
SAASMIG_SEVTIP_REVIEW: REVIEW: may be fine, but needs a person to decide — for example a function IBM lists as unsupported that the TM1 12 compiler still accepts.
SAASMIG_SEVTIP_INFO: INFO: nothing to do; worth knowing.
SAASMIG_TILETIP_DROPPED: Processes with at least one BLOCKER, outside TM1 Applications: the migration utility carries them over, but they do not compile or run on TM1 12.
SAASMIG_TILETIP_DROPPEDV12: Processes with at least one BLOCKER, outside TM1 Applications: they do not compile on this database.
SAASMIG_TILETIP_APPS: TM1 Applications (}tp_*) processes with a BLOCKER. TM1 Applications does not exist in TM1 12: retire it on the TM1 Applications tab rather than fixing them.
SAASMIG_TILETIP_FIXABLE: Findings this page can fix for you, with a preview, a backup and a rollback.
SAASMIG_TILETIP_USES: Processes and chores that call a process which will not compile on TM1 12, so the call fails there.
SAASMIG_TILETIP_USESV12: Processes and chores that run a process which does not compile on this database.
SAASMIG_GCLOUDHELP: Groups can be chosen and renamed the same way, through a }GroupProperties dimension and cube with a CloudID element. TM1 does not have them, so they are created here. Once a mapping exists, only groups with a CloudID value migrate, under that name; without it every group migrates under its current name. ADMIN, DataAdmin, OperationsAdmin and SecurityAdmin are always created on TM1 12.
SAASMIG_GCLOUDCREATECONFIRM: This creates what is missing: the }GroupProperties dimension with a CloudID element, and the }GroupProperties cube (}Groups × }GroupProperties). From the moment a group has a CloudID, the migration utility migrates only groups with a value. The Backups tab can take the new objects away again. Create them now?
SAASMIG_GCLOUDBLANKS: groups have no CloudID. Once any group has one, those will not migrate (the four admin groups are created anyway).
SAASMIG_GCLOUDALWAYSTIP: TM1 12 always creates this admin group, whatever the mapping says. A CloudID here renames nothing.
SAASMIG_GOTOAPPSTIP: TM1 Applications does not exist in TM1 12. Open the TM1 Applications tab to retire all }tp_* objects at once, rather than fixing them one by one.
SAASMIG_GOTOBEDROCKTIP: Bedrock processes are upgraded to Bedrock 5, or deleted when unused, on the Bedrock tab rather than fixed one by one.
SAASMIG_DELCHECKING: Scanning the model for anything that calls it…
SAASMIG_DELBLOCKED: Not deleted: these still call it. Fix or remove the calls first, then try again.
SAASMIG_DELNOCALLERS: nothing in the model calls it (checked on a fresh scan: processes, chores, and strings that name it).
SAASMIG_DELPOSSIBLEONE: 1 computed call could reach this process. Check it before deleting.
SAASMIG_DELPOSSIBLEMANY: {n} computed calls could reach this process. Check them before deleting.
SAASMIG_SPLITTIP: Drag to resize the two panes, or focus and use ← →. Double-click to reset.
SAASMIG_FIXEDNOTE: Apply cannot place this one, because the statement could not be rebuilt around it: paste it over the MDX in the process. It returns the same elements on v11, and it works on TM1 12.
SAASMIG_FIXEDNOTEJOINED: Apply does not write this one: the MDX is built from variables, so it cannot be run before it is offered. Paste it over the statement, and check that the process gives the same elements.
SAASMIG_FIXEDNOTECROSS: The MDX as the process assembles it, with the rewrite in place. Apply does not write it: it is built on several lines. Change those lines so they build this, and check the result.
SAASMIG_ASSEMBLED: MDX as the process assembles it, from
SAASMIG_COPYFAILED: The browser refused the clipboard: select the text and copy it by hand
SAASMIG_LOGELEMENTSECURITYFAILED: Element security of {dim} could not be read ({error}): its MDX was not checked against it
SAASMIG_GRANTREADFAILED: The element security cells for these groups could not be read.
SAASMIG_GRANTRULE: Cannot grant: rule-based security. A rule sets these cells in

SAASMIG_GRANTCONSOLIDATED: This is a consolidated element: these groups will see its total, which includes elements they cannot read.

SAASMIG_GRANTLEFTOUT: Not granted, because they cannot read any element under it (READ would show them the total and nothing below):
SAASMIG_GRANTNOBODY: Nothing to grant: none of the listed groups can read an element under it. Give them READ on the elements they should see first, or stop naming it in the MDX.
SAASMIG_DELNOTE: The whole process is saved to the Downloads folder first; the Backups tab restores it. Callers outside TM1 (PAW action buttons, TM1py, scheduled tasks) cannot be seen from here.
SAASMIG_DELDONE: Process {name} deleted. Its backup is in the Downloads folder.
SAASMIG_DELGONE: {name} is no longer in the model.
SAASMIG_LIVEWARNINGV12: This changes the live TM1 12 database. A fixed process compiles and runs again, and a fixed MDX subset returns what it did on v11. What a removed call did (switching logging off, saving data) is managed by TM1 12 itself — each finding says what, if anything, replaces it.
SAASMIG_HEADTIP_SELECT: Select the fixable findings shown ({n} objects). Shift-click a row's box to select a range.
SAASMIG_HIDDENSELTIP: These were selected under another filter. Apply selected includes them.

SAASMIG_UNSKIPTIP: Put this finding back in the list, the counts and the fixes.
SAASMIG_SKIPPEDTIP: Findings you skipped. They are left out of the list, the counts and the fixes, and remembered for this database in this browser (and in the project). Tick to show them again.

SAASMIG_APPLYNOTE_PROCESSV12: Writes to the live TM1 12 database. The process is backed up to Downloads and dry-run compiled first, and put back if anything fails.
SAASMIG_APPLYNOTE_SUBSET: Writes this subset's MDX to the live v11 model. The current MDX is saved to Downloads first; the Backups tab restores it.

SAASMIG_APPLYNOTE_VIEW: Writes this view's MDX to the live v11 model. The current MDX is saved to Downloads first; the Backups tab restores it.
SAASMIG_APPLYNOTE_VIEWV12: Writes this view's MDX to the live TM1 12 database. The current MDX is saved to Downloads first; the Backups tab restores it.
SAASMIG_APPLYNOTE_V11EFFECT: Until cutover, v11 runs without what was commented out; the finding above says what that changes.
SAASMIG_STEP2TITLE: Prepare the v11 model, in this order
SAASMIG_STEP4TITLE: Create and restore the TM1 12 database
SAASMIG_STEP1HELP: Scan model reads the processes, rules, subsets, views, chores and tm1s.cfg; nothing is written. The compile check is optional and needs a TM1 12 database connected in Arc.
SAASMIG_STEP3HELP: The utility turns this model into the TM1 12 backup file. After a fix in v11, scan and do these again.
SAASMIG_STEP4HELP: Outside the plugin, in PAW: Administration → Databases → Create, with exactly the v11 name; then Backup → Upload the .tgz → Restore. Connect the new database in Arc, then pick it below.
SAASMIG_STEP5HELP: On the TM1 12 database: what did not migrate, what does not compile, Bedrock, and the data files.
SAASMIG_STEP4LATER: Pick the TM1 12 database when restored
SAASMIG_STEPPLAN: {n} processes read files; the plan is shown
SAASMIG_STEPSAVE: SaveDataAll, so the utility reads every cube's current data from disk
SAASMIG_STEPCOMMAND: The command for the v11 host: open it to copy it
SAASMIG_STEPLOGREAD: {n} processes will not compile, per the log
SAASMIG_STEPCOMPARE: What v11 has that this database lacks
SAASMIG_STEPUPGRADE: {n} Bedrock processes to upgrade or install
SAASMIG_STEPGUIDE: How to do this step (user guide)
SAASMIG_LCOMPILES: Compile on TM1 12; some may still have BREAKS findings.
SAASMIG_LBLOCKED: Call a function TM1 12 lacks: fix before converting.
SAASMIG_LBLOCKEDV12: Do not compile on this database.
SAASMIG_LCALLERS: Run a blocked process, so they fail too.
SAASMIG_LBLOCKER: Migrates, but does not compile on TM1 12.
SAASMIG_LBLOCKERV12: Does not compile on this database.
SAASMIG_LBREAKS: Compiles, then fails or returns something else.
SAASMIG_LREVIEW: May be fine; a person decides.
SAASMIG_LFIXABLE: Of all severities: this page fixes it, with a backup.
SAASMIG_STEPFINDINGSTOTAL: {n} findings to act on, by group
SAASMIG_STEPBEDROCKUSEDG: {n} findings; all {b} in use, upgraded on TM1 12
SAASMIG_STEPMANUALG: {n} findings; {m} BLOCKER need a manual fix
SAASMIG_STEPFIXNONEG: {n} findings; nothing left to fix here
SAASMIG_STEP2HELP: The findings are grouped: TM1 Applications and unused Bedrock are deleted, not fixed; the rest are fixed here, by the object they are on. CloudID has to be ready before converting, because the utility reads it.
SAASMIG_SCANWAIT: Waiting for the database to answer
SAASMIG_NOTEFIRSTBODY: {pct}% of processes compile on TM1 12; {act} findings to act on, {fix} fixable here.
SAASMIG_NOTENOCHANGE: No change since the last scan.
SAASMIG_BYTYPETIP: {n} findings to act on, {f} of them fixable here. Click for the list.
SAASMIG_PRJINTRO: A project keeps this migration's scans, step status, results, backups and log in a folder you choose, so you can stop and continue later, or hand the work to a colleague. It is optional: without one, the plugin works as before.
SAASMIG_PRJNORECENT: No recent projects in this browser.
SAASMIG_PRJRECENTHELP: Remembered in this browser only. The list holds where each project is, never data or passwords. Removing a project from the list does not delete its folder.
SAASMIG_PRJNAMEHELP: Shown at the top of the page and in the recent list.
SAASMIG_PRJV12HELP: Add it when the TM1 12 database exists. A scan of it adds it, too.
SAASMIG_PRJFOLDERHELP: An empty folder, or a new one. Your browser asks once to let the plugin save there.
SAASMIG_PRJFOLDERBUSY: This folder has other files. The project adds its own files and folders and leaves the rest alone.
SAASMIG_PRJFOLDERISPRJ: This folder already holds the project {name}.
SAASMIG_PRJPLUGINFOLDER: This is the plugin's own folder. A reinstall replaces it, and Arc serves its files to anyone who can open Arc. Choose another folder.
SAASMIG_PRJERRFOLDER: Choose a folder for the project
SAASMIG_PRJKEEPSESSION: Add what this session already has: the scan, {b} backups and the log
SAASMIG_PRJCREATED: Project created. Scans, step status, results, backups and the log are now saved in {folder}.
SAASMIG_PRJCREATEDFILE: Project created and downloaded. It is kept in this browser; download it again when you stop, and open the file to continue elsewhere.
SAASMIG_PRJNOTPRJ: This folder has no project in it.
SAASMIG_PRJNEWER: This project was saved by TM1 12 Readiness v{v}. This is v{mine}. Update the plugin to open it.
SAASMIG_PRJBROKEN: {file} could not be read. Nothing was changed.
SAASMIG_PRJLOCKED: This project is open in another browser window. Close it there first.
SAASMIG_PRJPERM: {name}: your browser needs your permission again to save in its folder. Until then nothing is saved to it.
SAASMIG_PRJALLOW: Allow access to the folder again
SAASMIG_PRJDENIED: Access was not allowed. Nothing is saved to the project until you allow it.
SAASMIG_PRJMISSING: The project folder can't be found. It may have been moved or renamed.
SAASMIG_PRJUNSAVEDMISSING: Not saved: the folder can't be found
SAASMIG_PRJUNSAVEDERROR: Not saved: the last write failed
SAASMIG_PRJNOPICKER: This browser can't save to a folder here: Arc must be opened as localhost in Edge or Chrome for that. The project is kept in this browser instead: download the project file when you stop, open it to continue.
SAASMIG_PRJCLOSED: Project closed. Nothing was deleted: the folder keeps everything.
SAASMIG_PRJSHAREHELP: To hand the project to a colleague, copy the folder. It holds no passwords or connections, but it does hold the model's process code and the backups' original values.
SAASMIG_PRJSTALE: This result was read back from the project. Scan again before changing anything on the database.
SAASMIG_PRJBACKUPFALLBACK: Backup {file} could not be saved to the project ({error}); it was downloaded instead.
SAASMIG_PRJBACKUPGONE: the file is no longer in the project folder.
SAASMIG_BACKUPSHELPPRJ: Every Apply and every CloudID write saves the original first, into the project's backups folder. Restore puts those originals back on the database they came from.
SAASMIG_NOTEPROJECTBODY: Shown as it was saved. Scan again before applying anything.
SAASMIG_PRJFIELDTITLE: Start, continue or manage a project
SAASMIG_PRJHINTINTRO: Keep your work in a folder
SAASMIG_PRJKEEPSCAN: Keep this scan in a project
SAASMIG_DELUNKNOWN: Arc did not pass on TM1's answer ({why}), so whether this was deleted is not known. Scan again to see.
SAASMIG_DELSTOPPED: Deleting stopped: two answers in a row did not come from TM1 ({why}). Nothing more was deleted, and the backup holds everything. Scan again, then run it again.
SAASMIG_DELSIGNIN: Deleting stopped: {inst} answered HTTP {status} -- not signed in, or no rights. Sign in to the database in Arc, then run it again.
SAASMIG_DELTIMEOUT: no answer within the time limit
SAASMIG_DELNOIDS: Arc did not give the database's connection ids
SAASMIG_ONTM112TIP: Done after the restore: on TM1 12 the Data files tab uploads the file and points the process at it. Nothing to change on v11.
SAASMIG_NOTEPROJECTREFRESH: Refreshing it from the database: Apply is available once the fresh scan is in.
SAASMIG_STEPCOMMANDDONE: Copied: run it on the v11 host
SAASMIG_CMDTOOL: Utility folder on the v11 host (bin64)
SAASMIG_CMDOUT: Output folder for the .tgz and the log
SAASMIG_CMDDIRSHELP: Both optional, and typed: the browser cannot see the v11 host's disk. Without them, run the command from bin64 and the output lands there.
SAASMIG_VERDICTREADY: Clear to go: step 4 can start.
SAASMIG_VERDICTTODO: Step 4 can start, with {n} things to do:
SAASMIG_PRJHOSTPATHHELP: The folder's full path, typed once: the browser knows it only by its name. With it, the utility writes into the project's migration folder, and the plugin reads the log from there.
SAASMIG_CMDPRJASK: Where is {name} on the v11 host? Its full path puts the output in the project's migration folder:
SAASMIG_LOGFROMPRJ: Read the log in the project's migration folder
SAASMIG_LOGNOTINPRJ: {file} is not in the project's migration folder yet: run the command first, or pick the file.
SAASMIG_VERDICTTODO1: Step 4 can start, with 1 thing to do:
SAASMIG_V12PICKHELP: Once restored and connected in Arc, pick it here. Not listed? Add its connection in Arc first.
SAASMIG_V12ISV11: {db} is TM1 {v}, not TM1 12: pick the restored database
SAASMIG_V12REPLACE: The project names {old} as its TM1 12 database. Use {db} instead?
SAASMIG_ONTM112TIPV12: To do now: upload the file in the Data files tab, which points the process at it; the finding closes on the next scan.
SAASMIG_BEDROCKNOBUNDLED: This install has no copy of Bedrock of its own (Bedrock's licence keeps it out of the public release): Arc needs to reach github.com to compare Bedrock.
